victim.value: Aimee, a young woman shot twice in the face by her ex-partner Escue in a rage-fueled attack at a Quik Mart parking lot
victim.quote: He shot her twice in the face. Somebody somewhere began to scream.

culprit_and_motive.value: Escue, the culprit, killed Aimee in a jealous rage after she rejected him; The Jeepster (Leonard), her ex-lover, later possesses her body, driven by grief and inability to process her death
culprit_and_motive.quote: She rolled down the glass and gave him the finger...He had a .357 magnum in his hand.

investigator.value: The Jeepster (Leonard), the grieving ex-lover who pursues Aimee's memory obsessively, confronts those connected to her death, and experiences the crime as psychological devastation rather than as an external observer
investigator.quote: I can't be still. It's like I can't stand it in my own skin.

suspect_architecture.value: No traditional mystery suspect architecture. Perpetrator (Escue) is known from the outset — he murdered Aimee and killed himself. The Jeepster pursues peripheral figures (the Coors man, the counterman) as displaced targets of grief-rage, none of whom are genuinely culpable suspects in a mystery sense.
suspect_architecture.quote: I know Escue was broke and he borrowed ten bucks off the Coors man for the gas to get to where Aimee was working.

red_herring.value: No deliberate mystery-plotting red herring is present. The Coors man functions as a displaced target — The Jeepster irrationally assigns partial guilt to him — but this is psychological grief logic, not authorial misdirection planted to mislead a reader about the killer's identity.
red_herring.quote: You reckon that'll keep the dirt out of his face? I don't.

clue_fairness.value: Not applicable as a mystery convention. The text is a literary short story with no investigator and no withheld solution. The full account of Aimee's murder is eventually narrated directly to the reader in past-tense omniscient prose, but this is revelation of backstory, not fair-play clue placement.
clue_fairness.quote: For here's what happened, or what happened on the surface, here's what imprinted itself on the very ether.

social_world.value: Rural Southern underclass defined by drug economy, criminality, and decayed agrarian wealth. Emile's fall from prosperous farm family to meth cook maps the hierarchy: old land-owning class collapsed into poverty and addiction. Law enforcement (the cop father, deputies) represents institutional power set against this world.
social_world.quote: Once the scion of a prosperous farm family, now he could only look back on long-lost days bathed in an amber haze of nostalgia.

alibi.value: No alibi construction in the mystery-genre sense. Escue's crime is witnessed and he dies at the scene. The Jeepster's movements are tracked in real time. No character offers a false or verified whereabouts account that functions as a plot mechanism.
alibi.quote: He's broke. I don't think he's got the gas.

reveal_mechanic.value: No mystery reveal mechanic. The truth of Aimee's murder is delivered through direct omniscient narration mid-story, framed as the 'news the summer wind whispered.' The method is lyrical disclosure, not deductive demonstration — the reader is told what happened, not shown evidence to reason from.
reveal_mechanic.quote: For here's what happened, or what happened on the surface, here's what imprinted itself on the very ether and went everywhere at once.

media_and_audience.value: The crime radiates outward through community reaction rather than press coverage: cafe patrons avert eyes, the funeral home mobilizes deputies, the father's public cursing performs communal condemnation. The Jeepster is legible to everyone as a sign of catastrophe — 'the letter edged in black' — before he speaks.
media_and_audience.quote: He looked like the letter edged in black, the telegram shoved under your door at three o'clock in the morning.

investigator_wound.value: The Jeepster functions as an anti-investigator: his wound is total and constitutive. He is the cause of Aimee's vulnerability (he brokered her for money, failed to protect her, refused to loan her a gun) and now pursues a grief that cannot be resolved. His psychological damage is the story's subject, not a tool for detection.
investigator_wound.quote: I can't stand it in my own skin... I never knew you could feel like this. I can't be still.

_meta.title: Where Will You Go When Your Skin
_meta.author: WILLIAM GAY
